title: Console: resolve an app-relative push route in the native navigate listener, as the inbox does
body:
## Context

The push delivery contract merged in #29218 (`packages/spec/src/api/push-delivery.zod.ts`, around lines 28–39 and 82–83). It says `route` is the notification's `actionUrl`:
- either app-relative, `/opportunity/123`;
- or a Console route, `/apps/crm/opportunity/123`.

It also says the tap is resolved "as the inbox does, never verbatim": an app-relative path is hosted under `/apps/APP/`, and an `/apps/…` route passes through.

Nothing resolves it today:
- **Mobile shell.** It hands the route to the Console with the `objectstack-native:navigate` event, and on a cold start falls back to `<server>/_console<route>`. The shell has no app context and does no resolving. A search of `objectstack-ai/mobile` `main` for `resolveNotificationTarget` and app-relative hosting finds nothing.
- **Console listener.** `ui/packages/mobile/src/useNativeHost.ts:153-163` checks `isInAppRoute(target)` and then calls `navigate(target)` verbatim.

So a push for `/opportunity/123` falls to the Console's catch-all and lands on the home page, not the record. This is the defect objectui#5179 fixed for the inbox (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/appRoute.ts:328-399`, `resolveNotificationTarget`).

The bug is not visible yet, because no push channel delivers today (#29041). It will be on day one of push.

## Ask

1. In the native navigate listener, resolve the route with the same resolver every inbox door uses before navigating: `resolveNotificationTarget(route, hostAppSegment)`, as `openInboxNotification.ts` does.
   - `/apps/…` passes through.
   - `/{object}/{id}` is hosted under the current app, or the default app when none is open.
   - A route that resolves to nothing leaves the user where they are, rather than going to the catch-all.
2. The cold-start fallback in the shell (`location.assign` of the raw route) must not bypass this. Once the shell waits for `ready` (mobile #162, landed), the event path is the normal one. Confirm that the cold-start tap goes through the listener, and add a Console-side guard that resolves an app-relative path arriving as the initial URL.

## Acceptance

- Unit test on the listener: `/opportunity/123` with host app `crm` → `/apps/crm/opportunity/123`; `/apps/x/y/1` passes through; an unresolvable path does not navigate.
- The same resolver function is imported, not re-implemented.
